findings.where: Title-block nav, the 'MMM INFRA' home lockup (desktop-01 top left, phone-01 top left), and the Palette section (desktop-02, phone-01)
findings.fault: Mark's logo appears only recoloured in white linework: the wordmark is white rather than the logo blue #0070C0, and the arches are white rather than #404040. The palette never says what happens to those two fixed colours. It neither gives them a job as tokens nor declares them logo-only, so the tile has invented a reversed logo the client does not hold, and its colours sit outside the palette.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder. The logo is a fixed asset that 'stays', and a white version is made only with the client's yes. The layout and animation rounds need to know where the real blue-and-grey logo can sit on a diazo sheet. Here it never does.

findings.where: Article specimen heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop-02, phone-02), against the Type pair note 'Headings in ExtraBold capitals, tracked wide like a drawing title' (desktop-02, phone-02)
findings.fault: The article's title is set in title case with normal tracking. Every other heading on the tile (MARK M. MOSELEY, OVERPASS, CUT · MEASURED · EXACT, the section labels) is set in tracked capitals, as the type pair states. The tile states one heading rule and then shows its main reading page breaking it.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the designers of the layout round. They take the heading style from this tile, and it gives them two answers for the same kind of part, so a post's title will be set either way.

findings.where: Article specimen: the byline 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 • 18 September 2024' and the related item's 'Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF' (desktop-02/03, phone-02)
findings.fault: Like metadata is treated two ways. The byline date is written out in the sans, while the related item's date is ISO in Overpass Mono. One line also mixes two separators, a bullet then a middle dot. The type pair says mono is for dates, so the byline breaks the tile's own rule.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader of the article page would notice the mismatch. So would Angélique, who has to copy one format when she adds a post and gets two.

findings.where: Article specimen panel next to the Motion sketch panel (desktop-02/03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The two specimens sit side by side but are treated differently. The motion sketch, the texture panel and the related item each have a thin white frame. The article panel is an unframed fill in the same blue as the ground, so its edge shows only where the grid stops. On desktop that edge also starts about 4 px left of the column line that the 'AN ARTICLE PAGE' label and its rule sit on.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging the direction as a drawn sheet. On an engineering sheet every panel is ruled, and an unruled box with a slightly misaligned edge reads as a cut-out rather than a drawn panel.

findings.where: Texture panel on phone, the 'EARTH HATCH' and 'POCHE' samples (phone-01)
findings.fault: At phone width the panel loses its inner padding. The 'EARTH HATCH' label and its hatch box sit flush on the panel's left border, and the poche block runs into its right border. On desktop both samples sit inset inside the frame.
findings.who_objects: Anyone viewing the tile on a phone. The samples look jammed into their frame, which undercuts the 'measured, exact' character the direction claims.
